newsitem.title: UK: Britain's SAS commandos crack down on leaks.
newsitem.headline: Britain's SAS commandos crack down on leaks.

text.p: Former crack commandos who have written books about their exploits with Britain's famed Special Air Service have been banned from reunions at their old bases.
The ban, which covers Gulf War commander Sir Peter de la Billiere and best-selling "Bravo Two Zero" author Andy McNab, is aimed at plugging leaks about the highly secretive regiment.

A Defence Ministry spokesman said on Wednesday: "We will not admit to property occupied by the UK Special Forces any former personnel who have acted against the UKSF's best interests by publishing information about them."
He said soldiers considering possible memoirs might now be deterred by the prospect of being disgraced by regimental exclusion.
The banned soldiers will not be allowed to attend regimental reunions, weddings, funerals or Remembrance Day parades.
Comrades of the much decorated De la Billiere, who led Britain's troops in the Gulf War, called the ban petty and "a gross insult."
"This is a terrible humiliation for an officer of Sir Peter's stature," said Captain James Rennie whose own book detailed commando operations against Irish Republican Army guerrillas.
